content.title: About
content.content: Eggs are a nutritious food obtained from chickens. When fried in butter, the yolk stays runny or semi‑runny while the white forms a golden crust. This dish is commonly served for breakfast and is rich in protein, B‑vitamins, and healthy fats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggs are one of the most affordable sources of complete protein.
Butter adds a rich flavor and improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.
The yolk contains almost every vitamin the human body needs, including vitamin D, which is scarce in most foods.
The “sunny‑side up” method preserves more nutrients than fully hard‑cooked yolk.
Different cultures have their own ways to serve fried eggs: in Japan as tamago yakitori, in Spain as huevo frito.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A large egg provides about 6 g of complete protein, essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs supply vitamins B2, B6, B12 that support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Choline
items.content: The yolk is a rich source of choline, important for brain health and liver function.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Butter contributes monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin in the yolk help maintain eye health.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: The yolk contains cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume eggs in moderation.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked eggs can harbor Salmonella; use fresh eggs and cook whites until firm.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Frying in butter increases the calorie count, which should be considered in weight‑management plans.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the fried egg hot, seasoned with salt and pepper. It can be added to sandwiches, salads, burgers, or enjoyed with toast. For a softer yolk, fry over medium heat for 2–3 minutes; for a fully set yolk, cook 4–5 minutes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw eggs refrigerated at +1‑+4 °C in their original carton, usable for 3‑4 weeks. Fried eggs are best eaten immediately; if needed, cool to room temperature and store in an airtight container for no more than 24 hours.

ice-cream-cone-scooped-vanilla-waffle-co.title: Ice Cream Cone, Scooped, Vanilla, Waffle Cone

content.title: About
content.content: Ice cream cone is a classic dessert consisting of vanilla‑flavored scooped ice cream served in a crisp waffle cone. The vanilla taste comes from real vanilla beans or natural flavorings, while the waffle cone adds a light sweetness and crunchy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first waffle cone was invented in the early 1900s in the United States.
Vanilla is one of the most popular ice cream flavors worldwide.
Waffle cones can be slightly sweet or mildly salty, enhancing the ice cream’s flavor.
Traditionally the cone is served with chocolate sauce or sprinkles.

items.title: Moderate sugar content (when choosing reduced‑sugar versions)
items.content: Vanilla ice cream can contain less sugar than many fruit‑flavored varieties if a low‑sugar option is selected.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The dairy base of the ice cream provides calcium essential for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Dairy products contain vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Dairy‑based ice cream may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to milk should avoid this product.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The combination of sweet ice cream and a waffle cone adds significant calories, so portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hold the cone by the base and enjoy, allowing the ice cream to soften slightly to release the vanilla aroma. You can top it with chocolate sauce, nuts, or fresh berries for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the ice cream in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Keep the waffle cone in a dry place to maintain its crunch.

white-beans-from-dried-no-added-fat.title: White beans, dried, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: White beans are dried beans (commonly the Cannellini or Navy varieties) obtained after drying mature pods. They have a mild nutty flavor, a creamy texture when cooked, and a very low fat content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White beans are a staple in Mediterranean, Latin American, and Middle Eastern cuisines.
Dried beans can be stored for 2–3 years in a cool, dry place.
Soaking beans for 4–12 hours before cooking speeds up the process and improves nutrient absorption.
White beans are a popular plant‑based protein source for vegetarians and vegans.
In some cultures beans symbolize abundance and prosperity.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: One cup of cooked white beans provides about 15 g of protein, making it an excellent plant‑based protein source.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Dried white beans contain virtually no fat, suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Mineral‑dense
items.content: Beans supply iron, magnesium, phosphorus, and potassium, important for bone, muscle, and nerve health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine (B1), pyridoxine (B6) and folate support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Dried beans contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption; soaking and cooking lower its level.

items.title: Lectin toxins
items.content: Undercooked beans may retain lectins that cause gastrointestinal upset; always cook beans thoroughly.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to legumes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soak the beans, then simmer for 60–90 minutes until tender. Add them to soups, stews, salads, purees, or vegetarian patties. They can also be blended into a white‑bean hummus as a chickpea alternative.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. Properly stored, they keep quality for 2–3 years. Cooked beans should be refrigerated and used within 4–5 days.
